title: Chocotorta (Argentine no-bake chocolate biscuit and dulce de leche cake)

ingredients.name: chocolate biscuits (Chocolinas or similar plain chocolate biscuits)
instant coffee, dissolved in the milk
grated chocolate or crushed biscuits for the topping

steps: Beat the dulce de leche and cream cheese together until smooth and creamy.
Stir the dissolved coffee into the cold milk in a shallow bowl.
Dip each biscuit quickly in the coffee milk, just until it begins to soften, and arrange a layer of them in a rectangular dish.
Spread over a layer of the dulce de leche cream, then repeat with more biscuit layers and cream, ending with cream.
Chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until the biscuits have softened into cake.
Top with grated chocolate or crushed biscuits before slicing.

title: Fugazza (Argentine thick onion pizza from Buenos Aires)

ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more for the pan

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar. Add the warm water and olive oil and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Oil a rectangular baking tin and press the dough out to fill it, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons and toss with a pinch of salt and a spoonful of olive oil.
Heat the oven to 230 C. Pile the onions generously over the dough and scatter with oregano and olives.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the crust is golden and the onions are soft and starting to caramelise.
Cut into squares and serve hot, traditionally with fainá.

title: Jesuitas (Argentine ham and cheese puff pastry sandwiches)

ingredients.name: ready-made puff pastry, about 250 g each

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Cut each pastry sheet into rectangles about 8 by 12 cm; you need an even number.
Place ham and cheese on half the rectangles, leaving a 1 cm border.
Cover with the remaining rectangles, brush the edges with beaten egg and press with a fork to seal.
Brush the tops with egg and milk and sprinkle with a pinch of sugar.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm.

title: Picada (Argentine cold cuts, cheeses and olives sharing board)

ingredients.name: salame or other dry sausage, sliced
crusty bread and mustard to serve

steps: Slice and cube the meats and cheeses into bite-sized pieces.
Arrange them in groups on a large wooden board or platter.
Fill small bowls with olives, pickles and nuts and place them among the meats.
Add the eggs and bread, with toothpicks for picking.
Serve at room temperature with cold beer or red wine.

title: Pollo al disco (Argentine chicken and vegetables in a large wide pan)
steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, paprika and oregano.
Heat the oil in a very wide frying pan or paella pan and brown the chicken well on all sides. Remove.
In the same pan cook the onion, peppers and garlic until softened.
Add the tomatoes, potatoes, carrots and wine, then return the chicken, skin side up.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for about 45 minutes, until the chicken and vegetables are tender and the sauce is thick.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the pan.

title: Provoleta (Argentine grilled provolone with oregano)

ingredients.name: provolone or mozzarella (use a firm, melting cheese)
chimichurri or tomato slices to serve

steps: Heat a cast iron skillet or a grill pan over medium-high heat until very hot, or use a lightly oiled grill rack over embers.
Brush the cheese slices lightly with olive oil and place them on the pan.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the bottom is crisp and golden and the cheese is just beginning to melt.
Quickly sprinkle with oregano, chilli flakes and pepper.
Serve straight away in the pan with bread for scooping, as it hardens when it cools.

title: Revuelto Gramajo (Argentine scramble of fried potato matchsticks, ham and egg)

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Rinse the potato matchsticks and dry them very well.
Fry them in about 2 cm of hot oil in batches until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
In a wide pan, soften the onion in a spoonful of oil if using, then add the ham and peas and warm through for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and pour into the pan, stirring gently so they set in soft curds.
Fold in the crisp potatoes just before the eggs finish setting so they stay crunchy.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve at once.

title: Sándwich de bondiola (Argentine slow-roast pork shoulder sandwich)

ingredients.name: chimichurri, sliced tomato, lettuce or mayonnaise to serve

steps: Mix the garlic, oregano, paprika, oil, salt and pepper and rub all over the pork. Marinate for at least 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 160 C. Put the pork in a roasting tin with the beer and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for about 2.5 to 3 hours until very tender, then uncover and roast for 20 minutes more to brown the surface.
Rest the meat for 15 minutes, then slice it into thick slices or shred it.
Split the rolls, toast them lightly and pile in the pork with some of the pan juices.
Add chimichurri and your choice of fillings and serve hot.

title: Sándwiches de miga (Argentine crustless triple-decker party sandwiches)

ingredients.name: thin, soft white sandwich bread, crusts removed

steps: Spread each slice of bread lightly with butter or mayonnaise.
Lay out 4 slices and top each with ham and cheese, then cover with a second slice of bread.
On the second slice layer tomato, egg and lettuce with a pinch of salt and pepper, then top with the third slice.
Press down lightly, then wrap the sandwiches in cling film or a damp cloth and chill for 30 minutes to firm up.
Cut into 3 or 4 fingers or triangles and serve cold.

title: Sorrentinos (Argentine large round ham and cheese ravioli)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
tomato sauce or butter and sage sauce to serve

steps: Mix the flour, eggs and salt, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, ham, egg yolk, parmesan, nutmeg and pepper into a thick filling.
Roll the dough thin into long sheets. Cut 7 cm circles or use a round cutter.
Put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of half the circles, brush the edges with water, and cover with a second circle, pressing out the air and sealing well.
Cook the sorrentinos in boiling salted water for 4 to 5 minutes until they float and are tender.
Drain gently and serve with tomato sauce or sage butter.

title: Torta Rogel (Argentine layered puff pastry, dulce de leche and meringue cake)
steps: Make the dough by rubbing the butter into the flour and salt until crumbly, then mix in the water and vinegar until it just comes together. Rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 7 or 8 balls, roll each into a thin circle about 22 cm wide, prick with a fork and bake on trays at 200 C for 8 to 10 minutes until pale golden. Cool completely.
Layer the pastry discs with a thick spread of dulce de leche between each, pressing lightly.

For the meringue, heat the egg whites, sugar and lemon juice in a bowl over simmering water, whisking until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is hot to the touch. Remove from the heat and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Cover the stacked cake with the meringue and brown it lightly with a kitchen torch or under a hot grill.
Chill for at least 3 hours so the pastry softens, then slice.
